# Mātaṅgajātaka (Ja 497)

**ID:** Ja 497  
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Mātaṅgajātaka  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul14.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul14.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mātaṅgajātaka* (Ja 497) is a canonical Jātaka belonging to the class of early "ascetic poetry," in which the spiritual self-control and piety of a wandering ascetic are contrasted with the rigid ceremonialism of brahmans [Norman 1983]. According to the frame narrative (*paccuppannavatthu*), the Buddha related this story while residing at Jetavana with reference to King Udena and the Venerable Piṇḍolabhāradvāja, who was accustomed to spending the heat of the day in King Udena's park at Kosambī [Fausböll 1887]. The birth story (*atītavatthu*) recounts the deeds of the Bodhisatta as the outcaste sage Mātaṅga-paṇḍita and features the figure of Maṇḍavya, who is revealed at the conclusion of the story to have been a former rebirth of King Udena [Fausböll 1887]. The *Dhammapada* commentary also connects one of its narratives to the story of Jātimanta and the Bodhisatta in this Jātaka [Burlingame 1921].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Resembling parallels: SN 1.23 Jaṭāsutta; SN 11.19 Satthāravandanāsutta; SN 7.6 Jaṭāsutta

- [Fausböll 1887] Jataka Together with Its Commentary 4_ V. Fausböll, 1887 — Provided the edited Pali text, opening frame story with Udena and Piṇḍolabhāradvāja, and closing identification of characters.
